name: Can skin electrodes help predict chest vibration 80 ms ahead?
selection: Ten consecutive, previously unused post-music p-series participant IDs after excluding 001–003, already represented in the sensor viewer. Each integer ID denotes one person. Only one p recording per person. Reject duplicate waveform SHA256 among selected people or with b001/b002/b003. Record all same-file aliases from the release index without using them as observations.
source_checks: Require release SHA256 of each full .dat and .hea. Require the p header matching study phase and subject number, channel order I/II/RESP/SCG, names, signed little-endian WFDB 16, filename, 5000 Hz, four mV gains and baselines, frame count, exact byte length and all four full-record modulo-65536 checksums. Abort on mismatch. No annotation files.
sampling: Index native samples by i starting at zero (seconds i/5000). Convert per-channel (counts - header baseline)/header gain to mV. Filter each channel causally before decimating: for each endpoint i=20*k, take FIR-weighted samples i-200 through i inclusive using a unit-sum 201-tap Hamming-windowed sinc with cutoff 65 Hz at 5000 Hz. Endpoints on a 250-Hz grid, no delay compensation. Filter group delay is 20 ms. Never pad an unavailable observation. The released predictor consumes these endpoint-stamped mV readings.
calibration: For each participant including each held-out participant, compute channel means and population SDs on valid filtered readings at grid endpoints 60 <= t < 80 seconds. Calibrate ECG lead II, RESP and SCG independently. This uses past unlabeled sensor readings, including past SCG, to set units/offset at a new person. Require 4500 valid readings (of 5000) per channel and positive SD. Standardize by these means/SDs. Decode predictions to SCG mV.
trials: One fixed segment per person. Every 4 ms at forecast cutoffs 90 <= t < 120 seconds, predict the filtered SCG at t+80 ms (20 grid steps). Its entire native-sample support is [t+40 ms,t+80 ms]. Inputs end at t. No other trials or window search.
features: All models use only the history at or before each cutoff. Base ridge has 51 consecutive standardized SCG samples at lags 0..50 grid steps and 51 standardized RESP samples at the same lags, in that order from newest to oldest. Aligned augmented ridge adds 51 standardized ECG lead-II levels and 51 absolute first differences of standardized ECG II at those lags, newest to oldest (difference uses the preceding sample). No ECG I, beat marks or detection. The same ECG features delayed by exactly 1253 grid steps (5.012 s) give the misalignment control. Delayed ECG always comes from the same participant's actual past, without wraparound.
validity: WFDB -32768 is missing, invalidate filtered endpoints with any missing native count in their own channel's FIR support. Apply one common finite row mask across target, base, aligned ECG and delayed ECG for all scores and fits. Require at least 6750 paired valid rows of 7500 per participant; fail closed at this or any source/calibration gate without replacing people.
training: Three separate ridge fits: base, augmented aligned and augmented delayed in train AND test. Also test the already-trained aligned model with delayed test ECG for a substitution diagnostic. Fit each in float64 to standardized SCG targets, all coefficients penalized except intercept. Each training person has total weight 1/5, equal weights on that person's valid rows. Standardize each feature by training-weighted mean and population SD (constant scale becomes one); center target by its weighted training mean. Minimize weighted mean square error + 0.02 times squared coefficient norm. No tuning, selection, learned held-out coefficients or new participants. Persistence predicts the last observed filtered SCG at t.
score: Calculate RMSE in SCG sensor mV separately for every participant and model; count each held-out participant once. Primary paired delta is 100*(RMSE_base-RMSE_aligned)/RMSE_base per held-out person. Report unweighted mean, median, range, win count; list all five outcomes, per-model mean participant RMSE and within-person RMSE/SCG-calibration-SD; same paired summary aligned against delay-trained control and persistence. Descriptive support for incremental timing information here only if aligned has strictly lower mean participant-relative error against both base and delay-trained control and wins in at least 4 of 5 held-out people against each. Otherwise give the null/mixed outcome. Windows/grid ticks are serially dependent, never independent replication. No population or significance claim. No claim about physiological causation, subjective sensation, nerves, clinical diagnosis or treatment.
